endorsements.quote: These studies should adhere to the 2015 Standards for Reporting Diagnostic Accuracy Studies (STARD) guidelines in the absence of AI-specific reporting guidelines.

However, whether considering a pharmacotherapy, a physical medical device, or an AI technology, larger scale interventional clinical trials should ultimately inform decisions to implement healthcare interventions into real-world care.
Given the sensitivity of AI health technologies to their implementation context, it is also crucial that decision makers ensure that they are provided with evidence that addresses these issues.

unlisted_practices: Manufacturers should share study results openly to support better evaluation decisions across healthcare systems.

Researchers should design qualitative studies using stakeholder perspectives to generate evidence on the sociotechnical mechanisms by which an AI health technology influences outcomes in a specific healthcare context.
Researchers should pre-register clinical studies of AI health technologies and prespecify analyses and outcomes.
Researchers should design RCTs of AI interventions to reflect the intended real-world application as closely as possible.
Researchers should justify choices about how AI interacts with clinicians in a study, ideally through usability testing of different AI-clinician interaction protocols.
Decision makers should compare the capacity and expertise of real-world end users with those of users in the clinical study when appraising AI evidence.
Researchers should use AI-specific extensions of reporting guidelines (e.g., CONSORT-AI, SPIRIT-AI, TRIPOD+AI, DECIDE-AI) when reporting AI studies.
Organizations should invest in later-phase interventional studies such as RCTs of AI health technologies.

screen.reason: This article outlines good practice recommendations and frameworks for evaluating AI-enabled interventions across study design, conduct, reporting, and appraisal.
